---
id: dec-0061
kind: decision
title: Rebuild run state from the derived cache rather than from a written record
state: accepted
created: "2026-07-28T11:00:00Z"
tags: [fixture, enforcer, persistence]
alternatives:
  - option: replay an append-only journal at startup
    why_not: >
      replay cost grows with the length of the run, which is the cost a
      rebuildable cache pays once and then stops paying
    revisit_if: a run outgrows what can be rebuilt inside the startup budget
  - option: keep a written record of the last known position beside the cache
    why_not: >
      two records of the same fact drift apart, and only one of them has a
      reader that would notice
source:
  hook: manual
  tier: human
confirmed_by: human
---

Fixture entry for `internal/enforcer`, and the second half of E3-L4's
enforcement flip. `dec-0061` is what `dira supersede dec-0060 --with dec-0061`
installs in `dec-0060`'s place: afterwards the daemon plan is no longer cited
against `dec-0060`, and a plan proposing one of the alternatives above is cited
against this entry instead.

Its alternatives deliberately share no distinctive vocabulary with the daemon
plan, so that a check exiting 0 after the flip is evidence that `dec-0060`
stopped being enforced rather than evidence that this entry happens not to
match.
